text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- WTO reaches global agreement to deregulate telecoms.
-- Renault carmaker expected to post 1996 operating loss estimated at up to 2 billion francs, auto branch loss could reach 3 billion francs.
-- GAN executives say real-estate investments will probably weigh on 1996 accounts.
-- A majority of dealers on the Paris bourse are optimistic, survey shows, expect further rise of blue-chip CAC 40 index.
-- Snecma expects two years of strong growth, sees turnover rising to 13.8 billion francs through 1998 from nine billion francs for 1996.
-- The stability of the short-term rates is driving markets to record highs.
-- Compaq France to tackle small and medium-sized firms' market. Its servers account for 46 percent of the French market.
-- Global telecommunications market to be deregulated estimated worth some 3,700 billion francs.
